description.from:
Add an LLM distillation step that extracts a normalized structured artifact (entities + findings) from each accepted reference, embed THAT instead of raw composite text, and write the entities as filterable vector metadata. This is Cerebras's biggest accuracy win ("accuracy increased significantly when the thread was normalized into a consistent format") adapted to threat intel. Highest ceiling of all the epics; largest build.

## Current state (verified 2026-07-19)

- Distillation is ~40% built. `reference_summary` vectors already embed a composite: title + subtitle + canonical LLM summary + authors + sourceUri + first 2,400 chars (`_prepare_source_vector`, `src/papyrus_knowledge_query/vector_index.py:673-717`). The summary comes from `procedures/newsroom/reference_summarization.tac` and is read from the reference metadata attachment (`vector_index.py:857-874` region — locate `reference_summary_payload` resolution).
- ZERO entity extraction exists — grep for CVE in `src/` returns nothing.
- The persistence pattern to clone: `ModelAttachment` rows on references (see `src/papyrus_content/model_attachments.py`; summarization already persists artifacts this way). Versioning convention: `promptVersion` fields already appear in the summary payload metadata (`vector_index.py:784`).
- Ontology home for phase 2: `SemanticNode` (nodeKey, aliases, authorityScore) + `mentions` relation (`src/papyrus_newsroom/semantic.py:39`).
- Metadata sanitizer: `_sanitize_vector_metadata` (`vector_index.py:1275-1300` region) — verify it handles arrays of strings before relying on it.
- CLI patterns to clone: `references summarize` (find in `src/papyrus_newsroom/references_commands.py` / `reference_actions.py`).

## Design decisions (already made — do not relitigate)

1. **New procedure `procedures/newsroom/reference_distillation.tac`**, cloned from the `reference_summarization.tac` pattern (same model tier, same dry-run/persistence split — the CLI owns persistence, the procedure returns a payload).
2. **Artifact schema (versioned, `promptVersion: 1`)**: `{summary, key_findings: [str], cves: [str], threat_actors: [str], malware_families: [str], affected_products: [str], attack_techniques: [str], iocs: {hashes: [str], domains: [str], ips: [str]}, report_type: str, source_org: str}`.
3. **Anti-hallucination validation (non-negotiable)**: after extraction, every CVE, hash, domain, IP, and ATT&CK ID must appear VERBATIM in the extracted source text (compare after defang normalization: hxxp→http, [.]→., etc.). Drop non-matching values and log them. `threat_actors`/`malware_families` are exempt (aliases are legitimately inferred) but capped at 10 each.
4. **Persistence**: one `ModelAttachment` with role `distillation` per reference, JSON body, following the summarization attachment pattern exactly. New CLI command `references distill` with the same selection flags as `references summarize`.
5. **Index side**: in `_prepare_source_vector`, when a distillation artifact exists, embed `title + subtitle + summary + key_findings + entity lists (labeled)` instead of the current composite; otherwise FALL BACK to current behavior (corpus can be partially distilled). Write entity arrays into vector metadata as filterable arrays: `cves`, `threatActors`, `malwareFamilies`, `affectedProducts`, `attackTechniques`. Cap array sizes before writing (cves ≤ 20, others ≤ 10) — S3 Vectors has per-vector filterable-metadata size limits; the implementer MUST check the current AWS limit and add a total-size guard with truncation.
6. **Query side**: extend `_metadata_filter` (`services.py:397-433`) to map scope keys `cves`/`threatActors`/`malwareFamilies` etc. to `$in`-style filters, and pass them through `_normalize_request`'s accepted scope keys. This enables "everything accepted that mentions this actor" queries and feeds the scope-bundles epic.
7. **Re-run policy**: distill once per accepted reference; re-run only on `promptVersion` bump or `--force`. Cost is one-time per document and throttled by curation — this is our cost governor; keep it that way.
8. **Phase 2 (separate follow-up task, not this epic's DoD)**: emit `mentions` SemanticRelations to entity SemanticNodes.

## Files to modify

- NEW `procedures/newsroom/reference_distillation.tac`.
- `src/papyrus_newsroom/reference_actions.py` (or a sibling module) — distill action: fetch text, run procedure, validate entities, persist attachment.
- `src/papyrus_newsroom/references_commands.py` + CLI wiring — `references distill`.
- `src/papyrus_knowledge_query/vector_index.py` — read distillation attachment (mirror the summary-payload resolution), embed distilled text, write entity metadata with caps.
- `src/papyrus_knowledge_query/services.py` + `engine.py` — entity scope filters.
- Tests: entity-validation unit tests (hallucinated CVE dropped; defanged IOC matches fanged source), fallback-when-absent test, metadata-cap test, filter-passthrough test.

## What could go wrong

- **Hallucinated entities are the #1 risk** — the verbatim-presence check is the mitigation; do not ship without it. Log drop counts so prompt quality is observable.
- **Metadata size limits**: entity-rich references (vendor reports listing 50 CVEs) can blow per-vector filterable metadata limits and fail the whole put. The total-size guard with truncation is mandatory; test with an oversized synthetic artifact.
- **Embedding input changes → full corpus re-embed.** COORDINATE: batch this rebuild with the contextual-chunks epic (one re-embed, not two). Until the rebuild, old vectors serve fine (fallback path).
- **Partial corpora**: some references distilled, some not, for a long time. Every consumer must handle absence gracefully (fallback embed path, absent metadata keys).
- **Prompt/JSON failures**: the procedure must validate JSON shape with a bounded retry (the 3-attempt validation-retry pattern exists in `research_explorer.tac` — reuse it), and the CLI must skip-and-report failures rather than aborting a batch.
- **Tactus procedure conventions**: keep the dry-run contract (procedures never write records); persistence lives in the CLI action. Violating this breaks the newsroom's audit model.

## Out of scope

SemanticNode/graph emission (phase 2 follow-up), alias canonicalization across references, re-embedding the corpus (batched with contextual-chunks epic), any auto-acceptance of references.
description.to:
Add an LLM extraction pass that turns each accepted reference into a normalized structured artifact (entities + findings), embed THAT instead of raw composite text, and write entity arrays as ADDITIVE vector metadata. Cerebras's biggest reported accuracy win ("accuracy increased significantly when the thread was normalized into a consistent format"), refined by the extraction-prompt design in the Graph Engineering note (Cherny, July 2026 — independently compiled, not an Anthropic publication; see `docs/knowledge-retrieval-roadmap.md` §Graph engineering).

Entity RESOLUTION and graph promotion are a separate follow-on epic. This epic stops at per-reference artifacts + index integration.

## Current state (verified 2026-07-19)

- ~40% built already: `reference_summary` vectors embed a composite of title + subtitle + canonical LLM summary + authors + sourceUri + first 2,400 chars (`_prepare_source_vector`, `src/papyrus_knowledge_query/vector_index.py:673-717`). The summary comes from `procedures/newsroom/reference_summarization.tac`.
- ZERO entity extraction exists — grep for CVE in `src/` returns nothing.
- Persistence pattern to clone: `ModelAttachment` rows on references (`src/papyrus_content/model_attachments.py`); summarization already persists artifacts this way. `promptVersion` convention already appears in summary payload metadata (`vector_index.py:784`).
- Metadata sanitizer: `_sanitize_vector_metadata` (`vector_index.py:1275-1300` region) — verify array-of-string handling before relying on it.
- CLI pattern to clone: `references summarize` (`src/papyrus_newsroom/references_commands.py` / `reference_actions.py`).

## Design decisions (already made — do not relitigate)

1. **New procedure `procedures/newsroom/reference_distillation.tac`**, cloned from the `reference_summarization.tac` pattern. Keep the dry-run contract: procedures return payloads, the CLI owns persistence. Violating this breaks the newsroom audit model.
2. **Artifact schema (versioned, `promptVersion: 1`)**:
   `{summary, key_findings: [str], entities: [{name, type, description}], cves: [str], threat_actors: [str], malware_families: [str], affected_products: [str], attack_techniques: [str], iocs: {hashes, domains, ips}, report_type, source_org}`
3. **EVERY entity carries a one-line description grounded in that document.** This is non-negotiable and is the single most important schema element — it costs nothing now and is what makes the follow-on resolution epic work at all. String similarity cannot merge two aliases of the same actor with no character overlap; a per-entity description can. Entity `type` is a closed set: `THREAT_ACTOR | MALWARE | VULNERABILITY | PRODUCT | ORGANIZATION | TECHNIQUE`.
4. **Extraction prompt guidelines** (each addresses a known failure mode): extract only entities central to the document (controls recall); one-sentence description grounded in this document (enables resolution); prefer canonical vendor naming where evident (constrains vocabulary); never invent identifiers.
5. **Anti-hallucination validation (non-negotiable)**: every CVE, hash, domain, IP, and ATT&CK ID must appear VERBATIM in the extracted source text, compared after defang normalization (`hxxp`→`http`, `[.]`→`.`, `(.)`→`.`). Drop non-matching values and LOG the drop count so prompt quality stays observable. `threat_actors`/`malware_families` are exempt (aliases are legitimately inferred) but capped at 10 each.
6. **ADDITIVE ONLY (see initiative AD-2)**: entity metadata boosts and joins results; it is NOT a restrictive filter in v1. Extraction recall is unmeasured, and incomplete metadata used as an exclusion filter silently hides references the extractor missed. Expose entity fields as scope HINTS that widen or boost, never as `$in` filters that exclude, until recall is measured.
7. **Model tiering**: extraction is high-volume and schema-constrained — use the cheap fast tier. (Resolution, in the follow-on epic, needs the stronger tier.) Prefer a structured-output/schema-guaranteed call over parse-and-retry if the runtime supports it; otherwise reuse the 3-attempt validation-retry pattern from `research_explorer.tac`.
8. **Index side**: in `_prepare_source_vector`, when a distillation artifact exists, embed `title + subtitle + summary + key_findings + labeled entity lists`; otherwise FALL BACK to current behavior. The corpus will be partially distilled for a long time — every consumer must handle absence.
9. **Metadata caps**: cves ≤ 20, others ≤ 10, plus a TOTAL filterable-metadata size guard with truncation. Check the current AWS S3 Vectors per-vector metadata limit before implementing; an entity-rich vendor report listing 50 CVEs must not fail the whole put.
10. **Re-run policy**: distill once per accepted reference; re-run only on `promptVersion` bump or `--force`. Cost is one-time per document, throttled by curation — that is our cost governor, keep it that way.

## Files to modify

- NEW `procedures/newsroom/reference_distillation.tac`
- `src/papyrus_newsroom/reference_actions.py` (or sibling) — distill action: fetch text, run procedure, validate entities, persist attachment
- `src/papyrus_newsroom/references_commands.py` + CLI wiring — `references distill`
- `src/papyrus_knowledge_query/vector_index.py` — read distillation attachment (mirror summary-payload resolution), embed distilled text, write capped entity metadata
- Tests: hallucinated-CVE-dropped, defanged-matches-fanged, fallback-when-absent, metadata-cap/oversize, description-present-on-every-entity

## What could go wrong

- **Omission, not hallucination, is the bigger risk.** The verbatim check kills invented CVEs but nothing catches a prompt that extracts 3 of a report's 40 CVEs. This is precisely why AD-2 (additive-only) exists. Log per-document entity counts; spot-check a sample by hand before anyone proposes restrictive filtering.
- **Missing descriptions silently break the follow-on resolution epic.** Validate that every entity has a non-empty description; fail the artifact if not.
- **Metadata size limits** — see decision 9; test with an oversized synthetic artifact.
- **Embedding input changes → full corpus re-embed.** COORDINATE: batch with the contextual-chunks epic (one re-embed, not two). See the rebuild-coordination task.
- **Batch failures**: the CLI must skip-and-report per-reference failures, never abort a whole batch.

## Acceptance criteria

- Golden-set eval (see eval epic) shows no regression, and ideally improvement on paraphrase-category queries.
- Every extracted entity has a grounded one-line description.
- Hallucinated-identifier drop counts are logged and non-alarming on a hand-checked sample.

## Out of scope

Entity resolution, canonical nodes, aliases, graph emission (follow-on epic). Degree-based hub summarization (later follow-up). Restrictive entity filtering (blocked on recall measurement). The rebuild itself.
